overview: Hepatitis C is a viral infection that affects the liver, causing both acute and chronic illness, and can be life-threatening. It is spread through contact with infected blood and can cause liver cirrhosis and cancer. Hepatitis C can be treated and cured with antiviral medications, and early detection and treatment can prevent serious liver damage and improve long-term health.
symptoms: jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes)
diagnosis: nucleic acid test for HCV ribonucleic acid (RNA)
transmission: reuse or inadequate sterilization of medical equipment
transfusion of unscreened blood and blood products
injecting drug use through the sharing of injection equipment
sexual practices that lead to exposure to blood
prevention: safe injections and procedures in healthcare settings
screening of blood and blood products
risk_factors: men who have sex with men
people with signs of liver disease
people in prisons and other closed settings
key_facts: an estimated 50 million people have chronic hepatitis C virus infection globally
approximately 1.0 million new infections occur per year
about 242 000 people died from hepatitis C in 2022
